items.heading: eDiscoveryAI (EDAI)
items.text: eDiscoveryAI (EDAI) is a suite of generative AI (GenAI)-powered solutions that enhance document review and analysis. EDAI is available in TransPerfect’s Relativity Server and RelativityOne environments, with Reef Review availability planned for Q4 2025.
items.bullets:
EDAI Early Case Intelligence (ECI) is a cost-efficient solution that automatically generates high-level information about your dataset, including which documents are most likely to be relevant, case insights, lists of relevant keywords, document categories, and document types. It also produces a memorandum that summarizes the case issues and analysis based on a brief description of the matter and relevant issues.
EDAI Relevance is a GenAI-powered document review solution that lets counsel apply up to 15 prompts simultaneously to categorize documents by relevance, significance, or specific issues. It can be deployed in a variety of workflows, including first-level review, quality control review, or hybrid workflows combining technology assisted review and GenAI. EDAI Relevance can also analyze and review images (e.g., handwriting) and multimedia files.
EDAI Privilege is a GenAI-powered document review solution designed to identify documents protected by attorney-client, work product, and related legal privileges. It automatically generates privilege log descriptions for documents identified as privileged.
EDAI Privacy is a GenAI-powered solution that identifies, extracts, and redacts personally identifiable information (PII), including sensitive health information (SHI).

items.heading: Relativity aiR
items.text: Relativity aiR is a suite of GenAI-powered solutions that enhance document review and analysis. Relativity aiR is only available in a RelativityOne environment.
items.bullets:
Relativity aiR for Relevance is a GenAI-powered document review solution that allows counsel to use up to 10 prompts simultaneously to categorize documents by relevance, significance, or specific issues. It supports a range of workflows, including first-level review, quality control review, and hybrid approaches combining technology assisted review with GenAI.
Relativity aiR for Privilege is a GenAI-powered document review solution designed to identify documents protected by attorney-client, work product, and related legal privileges. It automatically generates privilege log descriptions for documents identified as privileged.
Relativity aiR for Case Strategy is a GenAI-powered solution that generates key deliverables based on the facts, people, and legal issues central to your case. Currently in a closed pilot phase, it’s expected to be available in Q4 2025.

items.heading: Cicero
items.text: Cicero is a document analysis and investigation platform that leverages the power of large language models (LLMs) and retrieval augmented generation (RAG) to help users summarize documents, conduct Q&A, create chronologies, and extract key data points. Users can ask unlimited questions (prompts) across their datasets and receive GenAI analysis and summaries with citations to the underlying documents to ensure defensibility.
items.bullets:
Summarization: Supercharge early case assessment. Quickly analyze lengthy documents and generate concise summaries and classifications that capture the essence of the content. Enable your team to grasp key points before diving into a deeper review.
Investigation: Find smoking guns in evidence. “Q&A” your documents to find the most pertinent information (e.g., “Is there any evidence that Dan harassed James?”). Evaluate case theories and narratives in real time against the evidence at hand.
Chronology: Save days synthesizing timelines. Scan any number of documents in moments to produce accurate and comprehensive chronologies. Edit, refine, and verify entries, then export to Word or Excel.
Extraction: Collate and compare key data. Choose the key data points and let AI tabulate your analysis across any number of contracts, records, or statements.

items.heading: Reef Translate
items.text: Reef Translate is TransPerfect’s proprietary Relativity application that streamlines the machine translation of large document volumes for eDiscovery. It enables rapid, on-the-fly translation of foreign language content within the Relativity platform, helping legal teams quickly understand the meaning of documents. Users can choose from various translation methods, including GenAI-powered translation.

items.heading: Image Analysis
items.text: TransPerfect uses a variety of GenAI and machine learning techniques, tools, and workflows to enhance image analysis—from object recognition to image labeling and captioning. Object detection recognizes objects present on an image (e.g., a human, a stoplight, a bridge) while image captioning and labeling can describe images and generate searchable text fields for further analysis (e.g., “The image shows a man standing in front of a whiteboard, writing on it with a marker. He is surrounded by a group of people sitting in chairs, attentively listening to his presentation.”).

data.title: End-to-End Digital Forensics: From Investigation to Remediation of Stolen Trade Secrets

items.heading: The Client
items.text: An international manufacturer engaged TransPerfect Legal’s global digital forensics team to support a federal litigation involving a former employee accused of sharing trade secrets with a competitor.

items.heading: The Challenges
items.bullets:
Conducting a pre-litigation forensic assessment of potential misappropriation
Preserving highly dynamic and sensitive data across multiple sources
Accurately forecasting project scope based on data volumes, formats and project objectives
Executing comprehensive remediation of misappropriated data from the competitor’s IT infrastructure

items.heading: The Solution
items.text: Given TransPerfect Legal’s global reach and deep expertise, the client selected our forensic technology and consulting team to lead both strategic and technical aspects of the trade secrets investigation.

items.heading: The Results
items.bullets:
Early forensic planning helped establish defensible preservation of sensitive data
Expert support strengthened the client’s legal position and rebutted opposing expert claims
Settlement secured full remediation of misappropriated trade secrets
Remediation was completed quickly, effectively and with minimal operational impact

items.title: Forensic Assessment
items.text: The engagement began with a planning session involving the client and outside counsel. Together, the team data-mapped the client’s IT environment and pinpointed where relevant proprietary information might reside – laying the groundwork for targeted investigation.

items.title: Preservation
items.text: Our licensed investigators then preserved a wide range of potentially relevant data sources tied to the former employee’s suspected misconduct. These early-stage efforts ensured defensibility and prevented any claims of spoliation, particularly important given the highly dynamic nature of the data involved.

items.title: Analysis & Testimony
items.text: To support budgeting and planning, we provided detailed project milestones and timelines. Our team also delivered forensic analysis, expert reports, sworn affidavits and testimony. data.title: Deploying On-Premise Digital Reef to Protect Confidential Data

items.heading: The Client
items.text: An Am Law 10 law firm representing the board of directors of a semiconductor manufacturer facing shareholder litigation.

items.heading: The Challenges
items.bullets:
Outside board members held highly sensitive, confidential information related to other business ventures that needed to be identified and excluded – without leaving the board members’ respective offices
Strict turnaround times for on-site processing, filtering and review in multiple cities on back-to-back business days, with the first deployment required within 48 hours
Each on-site matter involved distinct data sources and required customised workflows, including Digital Reef’s Pre-Review Analytics®, Cellebrite exports and Relativity review

items.heading: The Solution
items.bullets:
After initiating traditional forensic collections, TransPerfect Legal was asked to address unforeseen privacy and security concerns raised by certain outside custodians. In response, we deployed Digital Reef, our proprietary on-premise eDiscovery solution.
Our expert technicians arrived at the first custodian’s location within 48 hours, equipped with a mobile eDiscovery server. A customised workflow was implemented to accommodate the custodian’s specific requirements. The very next day, our team replicated the process in a second city for another custodian.
Once on-site, we conducted forensic acquisitions of the custodians’ mobile devices and webmail accounts. Due to the distinct nature of the data sources, two separate workflows were executed simultaneously using different tools.
After collection, the data was ingested into one of our on-premise eDiscovery servers. Mobile device data was exported directly into Relativity using custom Cellebrite scripts developed in-house, and loaded onto the mobile server’s Relativity environment for searching and data filtering. Meanwhile, webmail data was processed and searched using Digital Reef.
We then batched responsive data for on-site review by the custodian. A workstation was connected via a TransPerfect-managed mobile server, creating a secure local network for custodian review.
After the custodian and client’s legal team completed review and flagged sensitive documents for exclusion, final production sets were exported to secure external storage. We then forensically wiped the collection media, mobile server shares and both review environments to ensure complete data confidentiality.

items.heading: The Result
items.text: TransPerfect Legal successfully delivered a complex, high-security, on-premise eDiscovery solution across two cities on short notice – meeting aggressive deadlines whilst ensuring privacy, streamlining workflows, maintaining forensic defensibility, and controlling costs.

items.heading: The Client
items.text: A large US-based investment advisor under investigation by the Securities & Exchange Commission (SEC) for potential violations of federal recordkeeping laws related to “off-channel” communications – specifically mobile messaging. To demonstrate cooperation, the client agreed to collect and produce data from a broad sample of mobile devices, including the firm’s most senior executives.

items.heading: The Challenges
items.text: This matter posed several complex challenges. The scope involved over 50 custodians, requiring forensic collection of mobile devices nationwide on a compressed timeline. Amongst those custodians were C-suite executives whose devices contained sensitive personal data, which had to be carefully identified and excluded before any content could leave the client’s facilities. Compounding the challenge was the volume of messages – hundreds of thousands of records – that required a fast, defensible and privacy-conscious review to meet SEC expectations.

items.heading: The Solution
items.bullets:
TransPerfect Legal implemented a layered mobile collection and review strategy, leveraging proprietary tools and workflows to ensure speed, accuracy and privacy compliance.
Forensic Acquisition: We deployed forensic specialists to the client’s headquarters and completed a rolling collection of 50+ mobile devices in under two weeks. For executives, our team performed on-site exclusionary filtering to isolate personal content – preserving full device images on encrypted drives maintained by the client for defensibility. Remote custodians’ devices were collected using proprietary Mobile Remote Kits and iCloud backups.
Streamlined Review: The filtered data was ingested into TransPerfect’s Mobile and Short Message Viewer, a proprietary application within Relativity. Once loaded, we deduplicated messages across custodians, then applied threading and participant filters to quickly identify and prioritise relevant content. To protect privacy and accelerate review, semi-automated redaction was used to remove personal information – saving the client hundreds of hours of manual effort.

data.title: In-Study Interviews (ISIs) Amplify the Patient’s Voice and Augment Approval Timelines for Global Multilingual Research

items.heading: The Challenge
items.bullets:
A sponsor conducting global clinical research had plans to expand their initiatives across five new EU markets to streamline approvals and ensure that high-quality patient input aligned with regulatory expectations.
Post-study patient Interviews have historically been an afterthought or a “nice to have.” They are often overlooked or unplanned and often incur additional risks due to time and resource constraints and, most notably, financial costs. Furthermore, collected data is expected to be less dynamic than optimal, often augmented by subjectivity and challenges such as recall bias. Several additional key risk areas in interview design and conduct include test questions, data input errors, and data quality concerns.
In response, in-study interviews (ISIs), as opposed to post-study interviews, have become valuable for capturing real-time treatment data with thoroughly considered, pre-defined collection parameters, which reduce the risk of subjectivity or response shift and indicate safety signals.

items.heading: The Solution
items.bullets:
The sponsor, in conjunction with a COA subject matter expert (SME) from TransPerfect, worked to affirm the value of treating ISIs as part of the protocol design process. In this case, additional consideration was afforded to planning for in-person and remote interviews to account for cultural and geographical factors.
Study-specific countries and languages were triaged, accounting for established first patient-in (FPI) dates. Based on these, the team mapped out timelines and resource requirements for translating study questions, prioritizing individual languages based on FPI expectations. The team also consulted on selecting and scheduling in-person and teleconference interpreters to ensure smooth interview conduct. Diversity and patient cohort cultural origins were considered integral in all the decision-making processes.

items.heading: The Result
items.bullets:
The sponsor successfully conducted ISIs across five markets and was able to submit high-quality, real-world patient data to the regulatory bodies, which augmented submission approval timelines.
By proactively accounting for translation and interpretation requirements, the sponsor was able to mitigate risks associated with rush translations while keeping costs low.

data.title: Leading Pharma Deploys Successful Multilingual Multichannel Employee Training Program in APAC and EMEA Markets

items.heading: The Challenge
items.text:
A leading Pharma needed to train Korean and Japanese employees on a new SAP Master Data Governance platform. This was a complex training that required employees to review multiple documents, watch training videos, and attend live training Q&A sessions. The content within the training materials also required detailed planning and supplemental content adaptation services to successfully complete the localization.

With many moving parts to account for, alongside a tight timeframe to ensure teams received adequate training on the platform, the client needed to partner with an agile vendor who could translate with local team review before deploying the training program.

items.heading: The Solution
items.text:
The client selected TransPerfect to begin adapting the content and translating standard documents within their dedicated platform, leveraging desktop publishing and formatting tools. To adapt the video training content, the team translated and added subtitles in Japanese and Korean.

For the in-person training, live interpretation was provided for four sessions. The process and timelines for each project varied, requiring coordination between specialized production teams who worked in parallel on different aspects of the overall project. Progress and visibility into each stage of the project were tracked by weekly meetings held between the project management teams and the Pharma teams.

items.heading: The Result
items.text: Throughout the project, a total of 40,000 words were translated in under two weeks. This culminated in four successful live training sessions with accompanying documentation and training videos. The full process and multistakeholder review were completed within an aggressive launch timeline despite the inclusion of multiple reviewers and feedback loops. Due to the success of this rollout, the training program was expanded to additional regions in EMEA.

items.text: Laboratoires Vivacy was searching for a vendor to test the readability of their summary of safety and clinical performance (SSCP) information for patients (IFP), patient information leaflets (PILs), and instructions for use (IFU).

items.heading: The Solution
items.text:
Vivacy reached out to TransPerfect to recruit patients and healthcare professionals (HCPs) to review the SSCP IFP, PIL, and IFU. In order to gather meaningful insights from patients and HCPs, TransPerfect developed custom questionnaires for the users to complete while reviewing each document.

TransPerfect then compiled the questionnaire results into verification reports that validated user testing and provided key HCP and patient insights. TransPerfect also provided readability certificates for each document.

items.heading: The Results
items.text:
The project was completed successfully according to timelines, so Vivacy requested TransPerfect’s support on another user testing project involving both patients and HCPs.

As a result, Vivacy was able to validate that the SSCP IFP and PIL were reviewed by patients according to MDR requirements as well as gain HCP feedback to improve the IFU for physicians.

items.heading: The Challenge
items.text: Warner Bros. Discovery wanted to increase its production capabilities by targeting a four-week turnaround time for its localized series releases. Each series required subtitling and dubbing and continuity in character voices using specific talent; with over 10,000 minutes of content and 22 languages required, HBO Max was unsure where to turn.

items.heading: The Solution
items.text: TransPerfect Media, supported all requirements using our proprietary localization software, which could store all assets in one unified system to keep tasks on track and files secure. The team started by assigning specialized script translators who could adapt the scripts for cultural differences, and simultaneously monitored tasks and shared assets for the following steps. The translated documents were then reviewed by highly qualified translators for errors, and the studios began the dubbing process across five TransPerfect's owned and operated studios and a centralized subtitling team. Warner Bros. Discovery's key stakeholders then reviewed the localized content in-context using TransPerfect's proprietary tools, enabling direct input and feedback to the localization teams to accelerate the project turnaround time.

items.heading: The Result
items.text: HBO Max received high-quality and accurate subtitles and dubbing files for prompt international releases of some of its most popular series.

items.heading: Overview
items.text: Our text-to-speech (TTS) tool transforms written scripts into natural, lifelike dialogue tailored to specific project requirements. When paired with human review, it offers a powerful and cost-effective way to deliver high-quality, localized content for global audiences. Below are two case studies showing how TTS dubbing streamlined workflows and reduced costs—without compromising quality.

items.heading: Client One: Film Distributor
items.bullets:
THE CHALLENGE: A European film distribution company acquiring 60+ films per year for distribution in German-speaking territories wanted to explore AI dubbing as a way to reduce costs and optimize distribution in a rapidly changing market.
OUR STRATEGY: We partnered with the client on a pilot sci-fi title, designing a workflow that combined voice cloning, text-to-speech, and human post-editing. This approach delivered significant cost savings while preserving creative control. The client was closely involved in quality control and gave detailed feedback on voice tone and character consistency to ensure the final product met their standards.
THE WORKFLOW: Voice Creaton → Voice Added to GlobalLink → Audio Generation → Human Review → Audio Revision → Audio Import, Editing & Mixing → Delivery
RESULTS: Achieved a six-week turnaround time · Reduced dubbing costs by more than 50% · Maintained quality, with no rejections from platform partners

items.heading: Client Two: TV Broadcaster
items.bullets:
THE CHALLENGE: A broadcast TV company that had long partnered with our team for localization services faced shrinking margins as the industry shifted toward streaming. To continue delivering for the LATAM market, the client needed to cut dubbing costs by 30% while still meeting the rigorous quality and timeline demands of broadcast TV.
OUR STRATEGY: We proposed a hybrid workflow combining text-to-speech dubbing with human post-editing. This approach significantly reduced manual effort while maintaining human involvement at key points—including translation review, audio QC, and the creative mix. By ensuring human oversight on every piece of content, we demonstrated that automation could cut costs without compromising broadcast-quality standards.
THE WORKFLOW: Content Evaluation & Casting → Script Translation → Script QC & Preparation → Convert Text to Speech → Audio Import, Editing & Mixing → Human QC → Delivery
RESULTS: Maintained timelines and quality on par with traditional dubbing · Reduced dubbing costs by 40%, exceeding the client’s goal · Achieved zero rejections from broadcast partners

items.heading: Key Takeaways
items.bullets:
AI + Human Workflows Succeed: Hybrid workflows deliver significant savings while maintaining broadcast-ready quality.
Collaboration Builds Confidence: Close client involvement streamlines processes and builds trust in new technology.
Proven Quality for Top Platforms: Final products met the rigorous standards of major broadcasters and global streaming services.

data.title: Ethris Strengthening Clinical Operations with Trial Interactive
Ethris Strengthening Clinical Operations with Trial Interactive

items.heading: The Challenge
items.text: As Ethris prepared for their first clinical trials, they recognized the need for a more streamlined and future-ready approach to managing clinical recordation. Their internal processes for training and quality were entirely paper-based, with SOP training requiring in-person signatures and manual filing. On the clinical side, Ethris had no internal eTMF or eISF system yet, and they wanted to ensure full visibility, long-term access and proper oversight of their sponsor recordation.

items.heading: The Solution
items.text: Ethris selected Trial Interactive’s eTMF, eISF, LMS, QDMS, and TMF Services as a single, integrated environment to support both current needs and future expansion — a dedicated, sponsor-owned eTMF for consistent archiving, secure access and inspection readiness, and a true eISF environment with the ability to move records between eTMF and eISF.

items.heading: The Impact
items.text: Simplified training and record workflows: employees can complete training electronically, from anywhere, without in-person signatures or manual follow-up. Better preparedness for future growth: a strong, compliant foundation as the clinical program expands. Clear potential for greater efficiency at scale as Ethris moves into multi-site and multi-country trials.

data.quote: Having ownership and control over all active and archived eTMFs within a program is hugely efficient and beneficial for oversight and regulatory purposes.
data.attribution: - Nigel Tomkinson, Executive Director Clinical Operations, Ethris

items.heading: Overview
items.text: How Protas Revolutionizes Clinical Trials for Common Diseases with 100% Site Adoption of Digital Documentation

items.heading: The Challenge
items.text: As a new not-for-profit organization setting up foundational systems, Protas needed a document management solution that would align with their mission to make trials more efficient and accessible. Having worked with paper-based systems, the team knew the obstacles firsthand: storage and archiving issues, missing or misfiled documents, environmental costs and, critically, the lack of direct access to site documents between monitoring visits.

items.heading: The Solution
items.text: Trial Interactive provided Protas with an electronic ISF system, delivering a user-friendly platform that transformed how sites and central teams manage GCP essential documentation. The system enabled remote document review, real-time upload capabilities across multiple sites, and immediate identification of issues like duplicate documents.

items.heading: The Impact
items.text: Achieved 100% site adoption with overwhelmingly positive feedback on user-friendliness. Eliminated travel costs for document review — CRAs can now review ISFs remotely. Accelerated site setup timelines, enabled immediate detection and correction of documentation issues, reduced environmental impact and improved documentation quality.

data.quote: Using an eISF for the first time with Trial Interactive has been a really positive experience. It saves a lot of time, it increases the quality of what’s happening, and because it’s such a user-friendly interface, it’s really well received by sites and by central staff.
data.attribution: - Jen Dumbleton, Head of Trial Management and Product Owner, Protas
